---
title: "Shared FMD Project color palette"
output: html_notebook
---

**Purpose:** use the same nine colors across every chart. AI/AN-alone and other
single-race respondents always use the same two contrasting colors; other
colors are reserved for models, risk categories, and visual emphasis.

This module changes **presentation only**, never survey data, model fitting,
probabilities, group definitions, or performance metrics. The custom scales
are applied explicitly in each notebook to prevent inconsistent automatic
colors when one group or category is absent.

## Palette, scales, and chart theme

```{r shared-plot-palette}
# Use the exact nine supplied colors with descriptive, reusable names.
atg_palette <- c(
    rose = "#c98389",
    burgundy = "#954e4b",
    peach = "#febd97",
    sand = "#d6c6bc",
    gold = "#c3a052",
    mauve = "#82667a",
    turquoise = "#33c2b1",
    evergreen = "#125238",
    rust = "#aa663c"
)

# Use the requested turquoise, rust, and gold colors for the main populations.
atg_group_colors <- c(
    "AI/AN alone" = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
    "Other identified single-race" = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    "Unresolved/multiracial" = atg_palette[["gold"]]
)

# Keep algorithm colors fixed across year and evaluation notebooks.
atg_model_colors <- c(
    logistic = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    lasso = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
    forest = atg_palette[["gold"]],
    prevalence_only = atg_palette[["evergreen"]]
)

# Feature names match the actual harmonized predictors, not causal constructs.
atg_feature_colors <- c(
    physical_days_group = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
    general_health_group = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    AGE_BAND = atg_palette[["gold"]],
    SEX_CLEAN = atg_palette[["rose"]],
    EDU_CLEAN = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
    INCOME_BAND = atg_palette[["gold"]]
)

atg_predictor_group_colors <- c(
    physical_only = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
    social_demographic_only = atg_palette[["gold"]],
    combined = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    historical_average = atg_palette[["evergreen"]]
)

atg_version_colors <- c(
    raw = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    calibrated = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]
)

atg_measure_colors <- c(
    prevalence = atg_palette[["rust"]],
    mean_prediction = atg_palette[["gold"]]
)

atg_year_colors <- c(
    `2023` = atg_palette[["gold"]],
    `2025` = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]
)

# A restrained publication-style theme for readable, accessible charts.
atg_theme <- function() {
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        ggplot2::theme(
            plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(
                color = atg_palette[["rust"]],
                face = "bold",
                size = 13
            ),
            plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(
                color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
                size = 10
            ),
            plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(
                color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
                size = 9
            ),
            axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]),
            axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(color = atg_palette[["rust"]]),
            legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
            legend.position = "bottom",
            panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(
                color = "#e6dfdb",
                linewidth = 0.3
            ),
            plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
        )
}

atg_scale_color_groups <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = atg_group_colors, na.value = atg_palette[["sand"]])
}

atg_scale_fill_groups <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_group_colors, na.value = atg_palette[["sand"]])
}

atg_scale_color_models <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = atg_model_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_models <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_model_colors)
}

atg_scale_color_features <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = atg_feature_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_features <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_feature_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_predictor_groups <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_predictor_group_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_versions <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_version_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_measures <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_measure_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_years <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_year_colors)
}

atg_scale_fill_flags <- function() {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(`FALSE` = atg_palette[["sand"]], `TRUE` = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]),
        labels = c(`FALSE` = "Other candidate", `TRUE` = "Selected model")
    )
}

# Deterministic category mapping: the literal "Missing" stays sand across charts.
# Each named BRFSS response category receives a fixed color, independent of order.
atg_category_colors <- function(values) {
    labels <- sort(unique(as.character(values)))
    labels <- labels[!is.na(labels)]
    fallback <- c(
        atg_palette[["turquoise"]], atg_palette[["rust"]],
        atg_palette[["gold"]], atg_palette[["evergreen"]],
        atg_palette[["rose"]], atg_palette[["peach"]],
        atg_palette[["burgundy"]], atg_palette[["mauve"]]
    )
    colors <- stats::setNames(rep(fallback, length.out = length(labels)), labels)
    fixed <- c(
        `0` = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
        `1-6` = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
        `7-13` = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        `14-20` = atg_palette[["peach"]],
        `21-30` = atg_palette[["rust"]],
        `<25k` = atg_palette[["rust"]],
        `25-49k` = atg_palette[["rust"]],
        `50-74k` = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        `75k+` = atg_palette[["turquoise"]],
        Missing = atg_palette[["sand"]]
    )
    known <- intersect(labels, names(fixed))
    colors[known] <- fixed[known]
    colors
}

atg_scale_fill_categories <- function(values) {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = atg_category_colors(values))
}
```
